## Overview

This analysis produces **national estimates of plant species' trait means** for
Australia, as part of the ARDC-funded AusTraits programme. Trait data are sampled
unevenly across each species' geographic and climatic range, so a simple average
is biased toward wherever a species happened to be measured. Instead, for each
trait we estimate the species-level mean **at the centre of the species' climate
distribution** (the 2D precipitation–temperature medoid), giving a consistent,
defensible reference point across species and traits.

We use a hierarchical within-group-centred model. Predictors are centred on the
medoid (`x_c = obs − medoid`), so the between-species terms describe turnover
across the continent and the within-species terms describe how a trait shifts
across a species' range. This serves two goals: (1) delivering the species-mean
estimates for AusTraits, and (2) underpinning a paper that reports these means
and gives credence to the estimates (uncertainty intervals, the within/between
decomposition, and — via the BRMS backend — full posterior inference). See
`demo.qmd` for the statistical motivation and `refactor_plan.md` for the design.

The dataset (`dataset_construction.qmd`) combines plant height from AVH with the
remaining traits from AusTraits. Two interchangeable fitting backends are
available — `tmb` (fast, used here) and `brms` (full posterior) — behind one
interface (`fit_trait_climate_model()`); all logic lives in `R/`.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
library(glmmTMB)
library(broom.mixed)
library(easystats)

source("R/init.R")

update <- FALSE
out_dir <- "outputs/traits"
```

```{r load-data}
data_unified <- arrow::read_parquet("data-processed/data_traits_climate_unified.parquet")
```

## Fit per-trait models

One model per trait (TMB), keeping species with more than `n_min` records. Each
fit yields the species-level trait value at the climate centre, exported to
`outputs/traits/<trait>_climate_response.csv.gz` (with a `_meta.csv` dictionary).

```{r fit-traits}
summary_file <- file.path(out_dir, "trait_model_summary.csv")

if (update || !file.exists(summary_file)) {
  fits <- run_trait_models(data_unified, backend = "tmb", n_min = 5, out_dir = out_dir)
  trait_summary <- summarise_trait_fits(fits)
  readr::write_csv(trait_summary, summary_file)
} else {
  trait_summary <- readr::read_csv(summary_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
}
```

### Full posterior (BRMS backend, opt-in)

For the deliverable we refit with the BRMS backend to get full posterior
inference. It shares the same interface; each fit uses 4 chains with within-chain
threading and is cached to disk (reused unless the model/data change). BRMS is
slow at scale (≈1 min per few-hundred-species trait; tens of minutes for height),
so it is opt-in (`eval=FALSE`) — run it deliberately, not on every render. Always
inspect the diagnostics: larger traits need more iterations (e.g. `leaf_area` did
not converge at `iter = 1500`). One-time `cmdstanr::rebuild_cmdstan()` resolves
stale precompiled-header warnings when threading first turns on.

```{r fit-brms, eval = FALSE}
setup_parallel()  # macOS-safe multisession (not used by brms itself, but harmless)

fits_brms <- run_trait_models(
  data_unified, backend = "brms", n_min = 5, out_dir = out_dir,
  fits_dir = "data-processed/brms_fits",
  threads = 2, iter = 2000, warmup = 1000, refresh = 0, silent = 2
)

# Convergence summary; refit any flagged trait with more iterations.
brms_diag <- summarise_trait_diagnostics(fits_brms)
readr::write_csv(brms_diag, file.path(out_dir, "brms_diagnostics.csv"))
brms_diag |> knitr::kable()
```

### Fitted fixed effects by trait

Between-species (`_mn`) and within-species (`_c`) slopes for precipitation and
temperature, plus the global intercept, for each trait.

```{r summary-table}
trait_summary |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Across-species turnover

For each trait, the predicted species mean at the climate centre against the
centre's mean annual precipitation (log–log), with the across-species trend.
Figures are written (PNG + PDF) to `outputs/traits/figures/`.

```{r centre-figures, results = "asis"}
traits <- trait_summary$trait
fig_dir <- file.path(out_dir, "figures")

for (tr in traits) {
  f <- file.path(out_dir, paste0(clean_species_filename(tr), "_climate_response.csv.gz"))
  if (!file.exists(f)) next
  centres <- readr::read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE)
  p <- plot_trait_centres(centres, tr, x = "precip", log_y = TRUE)
  paths <- save_figure(p, file.path(fig_dir, clean_species_filename(tr)), width = 7, height = 5)
  cat("\n\n### ", tr, "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat("![", tr, "](", paths[["png"]], ")\n\n", sep = "")
}
```

## Round 2: simple means + combined product

The climate-centre model (round 1) covers species with enough records *and* a
climate medoid. For the remainder — low-coverage species, and species dropped for
having no medoid — we fall back to a simple per-species mean (the geometric mean
of all available records, since traits are log-normal). These run on the full,
un-medoid-filtered record pool, so every species with any data gets an estimate.

The combined product gives one **best estimate** per species × trait: the
climate-centre estimate where available, otherwise the simple mean, with a
`method` flag recording which was used.

```{r round2-means}
records_all <- dplyr::bind_rows(load_height_records(), load_austraits_records())
simple_means <- estimate_simple_means(records_all)

centre_estimates <- load_centre_estimates(sort(unique(simple_means$trait_name)), dir = out_dir)
combined <- combine_estimates(simple_means, centre_estimates)

readr::write_csv(combined, file.path(out_dir, "species_trait_means_combined.csv.gz"))
```

### Coverage by method

How many species per trait are estimated by the climate-centre model vs the
simple-mean fallback.

```{r coverage}
combined |>
  count(trait_name, method) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = method, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  dplyr::mutate(total = climate_centre + simple_mean) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Exported files

Per trait, in `outputs/traits/`:

- `<trait>_climate_response.csv.gz` — round-1 climate-centre estimates: one row
  per species with the predicted trait value at the climate centre (with
  interval), the centre climate, sample size, and species random effects.
- `<trait>_climate_response_meta.csv` — a column dictionary.
- `trait_model_summary.csv` — fitted fixed effects for every trait.
- `species_trait_means_combined.csv.gz` — the integrated best-estimate product
  across all traits: climate-centre estimate where available, else the simple
  mean, with a `method` flag.
